extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusion, and agreed sanctions for a registered patent attorney who committed a felony, including suspension, reinstatement procedures, probation, publication, and procedural enforcement steps under applicable USPTO rules and statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly cites these statutory and regulatory provisions as the legal foundation for the disciplinary proceeding and the Director's authority to approve the settlement agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribing committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on the practitioner's honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admits he violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) by committing the criminal act of online solicitation of a minor for sexual conduct (a felony), as evidenced by his plea in The State of Texas v. Robert Bohanek.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and scope of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for five years, said period of suspension to run from August 19, 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension covers all practice before the USPTO (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) and is tied to a specific effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing petition for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after thirty-six (36) months from August 19, 2014, Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 requesting reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the suspension is five years, the practitioner may seek reinstatement after 36 months in accordance with the cited regulatory petition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension remains until formal reinstatement under § 11.60(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark and other non-patent matters until the OED Director grants a petition reinstating Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is a formal grant by the OED Director under the regulatory standard; mere passage of time does not automatically terminate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires adherence to the regulatory duties applicable to suspended practitioners (the order cites the regulation but does not restate its text).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly directs the OED Director to follow the referenced regulation (procedural duties by the Office) in carrying out the Order; the order does not restate the regulation's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps to sever the respondent's access/association with USPTO electronic accounts and certificates are required immediately upon the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While suspended, the practitioner is barred from seeking new USPTO customer credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is reinstated to practice before the USPTO, he shall serve a probationary period until May 28, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets a specific probation end date tied to the underlying criminal adjudication; probation conditions apply after reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice during probation and revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark and other non-patent law during his probationary period, unless his probation is revoked and he is suspended by order of the USPTO Director or otherwise no longer has the authority to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation allows practice subject to continued compliance; violation can trigger immediate suspension or revocation of authority to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during the probationary period, the OED Director shall: (1) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order immediate suspension for up to six months; (2) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record furnished under 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and (3) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order prescribes the sequential procedural steps, service method (address of record), and a 15-day response period for probation enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director requesting immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day response period the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause; (ii) Respondent's response, if any; and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the opinion, and request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend Respondent for up to six months for the violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order establishes the evidence-and-record referral package the OED Director must send to the USPTO Director to seek an immediate short suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the referral and Respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not stay the suspension; suspension goes into effect notwithstanding appeal/review proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room, which is publicly accessible through the Office's website at: http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires public posting of the disciplinary decision on the Office's electronic reading room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette with specified content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Suspension and Probation. The notice shall identify the respondent, state he was suspended on an interim basis, state the rule violated (USPTO Rule of Professional Conduct 11.804(b)), summarize the underlying criminal conviction (online solicitation of a minor for sexual conduct, a felony), note the suspension, and state that the action is the result of a settlement agreement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26, and 11.59; it shall also reference the OED Reading Room location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies exact content elements to be included in the Gazette notice and ties the publication to statutory/regulatory authorities and the public reading room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order preserves the Office's ability to use the disciplinary record as aggravation or rebuttal in future matters involving the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to dismiss pending disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion with the administrative law judge requesting the dismissal of the pending disciplinary proceeding within fourteen (14) days of the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following approval of the settlement and issuance of the Final Order, OED is required to seek dismissal of any parallel pending disciplinary proceeding within a 14-day deadline.
